neighbours.label: a temporal anchor in historical narrative ('since the 1960s', 'after the end of', 'soon after the 1953 ...')
fire: Doctors had known about the fever since the 1870s, though few studied it.
The suburb expanded quickly after the end of the Korean War, and shops followed.
Burr enlisted with the militia following the battle at Saratoga in the autumn of 1777.
The agency started its secret programme soon after the 1953 coup in Tehran.
The firm was established in 1908 by a pair of engineers from Glasgow.
Railways had been spreading across the region since the middle of the 19th century.
The league collapsed soon after the 1929 crash, and its clubs folded.
Interest in the ruins has grown steadily since the end of the Second World War.
quiet: Doctors had many theories about the fever, though few studied it.
The suburb expanded quickly along the new railway line, and shops followed.
Burr enlisted with the militia because his brothers had joined it too.
The agency runs a secret programme from an office in Tehran.
The firm is owned by a pair of engineers from Glasgow.
Railways are spreading across the region, and the map keeps changing.
The league collapsed under heavy debts, and its clubs folded.
Interest in the ruins has grown steadily among students of archaeology.
